title: Intercept Form of a Line
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A line has a nonzero x-intercept a and a nonzero y-intercept b. Derive the equation of the line in the symmetric intercept form and verify it passes through both intercept points.

steps.title: Identify the Two Defining Points
steps.explanation: The x-intercept a means the line meets the x-axis at (a, 0); the y-intercept b means it meets the y-axis at (0, b). Two distinct points determine the line.
steps.why: A nonzero condition on a and b keeps the two points distinct and off the origin overlap, so the slope is well defined.

steps.title: Compute the Slope
steps.explanation: Rise over run between the intercept points gives the slope -b/a.
steps.why: The slope formula applied to (a, 0) and (0, b) directly yields the negative ratio of the intercepts.

steps.title: Rearrange into Intercept Form
steps.explanation: Point-slope form through (a, 0) expands to y = b - (b/a)x; dividing by b and collecting terms produces the symmetric equation.
steps.why: Algebraic normalization by b turns the two-intercept data into a single scale-free identity in x/a and y/b.

steps.title: Verify Both Intercepts
steps.explanation: Substituting either intercept point into x/a + y/b makes exactly one fraction equal to 1 and the other equal to 0, satisfying the equation.
steps.why: Direct substitution is the definitive membership test for a point and its candidate line.
